blocks.text: # Glossary
**First crack** is the audible popping when steam escapes the bean.
**Charge** is the moment green coffee enters the hot drum.
**Drop** is the moment roasted coffee leaves the drum.
**Bloom** is the release of carbon dioxide when water first touches fresh grounds.
**Chaff** is the papery skin that separates from the bean during roasting.
Note: always check the drum temperature before charging.
**Drop** is the moment roasted coffee leaves the drum.

# Grinders
Burr grinders give a consistent particle size. Flat burrs are used for [espresso](espresso.md) and conical burrs for filter.
## Calibration
Grind size is adjusted daily. A finer grind slows the shot, a coarser grind speeds it up.
## Cleaning
Grinders are cleaned weekly with rice-free cleaning tablets.

# Maintenance
Regular maintenance keeps the equipment safe.
## Daily
- Backflush the espresso machine with a blind basket.
- Empty the chaff collector of the roaster.
## Monthly
- Descale the espresso machine boiler.
- Inspect the roaster exhaust for build-up.
Note: always check the drum temperature before charging.
## Checklist

# Roasting
Roasting turns green coffee into the brown beans we grind. The roaster controls heat, airflow and time, and every batch is logged in [[r005-roast-log#Roast Log]].
## Stages
1. Drying: moisture leaves the bean until it turns yellow.
2. Maillard: sugars and amino acids react and aromas develop. - The bean expands and the color moves to tan. - Most body is built here.
3. Development: the time after first crack that sets acidity.
## Profiles
Light profiles keep floral notes and are used for [[origins]]. Dark profiles mute acidity and suit ![[espresso]].
> Never roast two origins in the same drum without a cleaning cycle.
Note: always check the drum temperature before charging.

# Espresso
Espresso is brewed with nine bars of pressure for about 28 seconds.
## Recipe
- Dose: 18 g
- Yield: 36 g
- Time: 26 to 30 seconds - Under 24 seconds tastes sour. - Over 32 seconds tastes bitter.
## Equipment
The shop uses a two-group machine that is descaled every month according to [maintenance hakkında](r004-maintenance.md).

```python
def ratio(dose, yield_):
    return yield_ / dose  # 1:2 is the house standard
```
The house blend is defined in [[blends]].

# Safety
Roasting produces smoke and heat; the exhaust must be inspected according to [[r004-maintenance]].
## Fire
Chaff can ignite. Keep a class D extinguisher next to the roaster and never leave a batch unattended.
## Burns
The drum and the steam wand are hot. Use gloves when emptying the cooling tray.
Emergency number: 112

# Cupping
Cupping is the standard tasting protocol used to evaluate lots.
## Protocol
1. Grind 8.25 g of coffee per 150 ml of water.
2. Smell the dry grounds.
3. Pour water at 93 °C and wait four minutes.
4. Break the crust and skim.
5. Slurp from a spoon and score.
## Scoring
Scores cover fragrance, flavor, aftertaste, acidity, body and balance. Lots under 84 points are rejected. Results are stored next to the [[r005-roast-log|roast-log notu]].

# Filter Coffee
Filter coffee uses a 1:16 ratio of coffee to water.
## Pour over
- Rinse the paper filter.
- Bloom with twice the coffee weight in water for 30 seconds.
- Pour in slow circles until the target weight.
Colombian lots from [origins](origins.md) are the default filter offering. The grinder setting is described in [grinders hakkında](r002-grinders.md).

# Origins
We buy from three producing regions. Each lot is cupped before purchase, following ![[r007-cupping]].
## Ethiopia
Guji and Yirgacheffe lots are washed and show jasmine and bergamot. They are roasted light, see ![[roasting]].
## Colombia
Huila lots are balanced, with red apple and panela sweetness. They work as filter and as [[espresso#Espresso]].
## Brazil
Cerrado naturals are nutty and low in acidity. They form the base of the house blend described in [blends hakkında](blends.md).

# Roasting
Roasting turns green coffee into the brown beans we grind. The roaster controls heat, airflow and time, and every batch is logged in [[r005-roast-log#Roast Log]].
## Stages
1. Drying: moisture leaves the bean until it turns yellow.
2. Maillard: sugars and amino acids react and aromas develop. - The bean expands and the color moves to tan. - Most body is built here.
3. Development: the time after first crack that sets acidity.
## Profiles
Light profiles keep floral notes and are used for [[origins]]. Dark profiles mute acidity and suit ![[espresso]].
> Never roast two origins in the same drum without a cleaning cycle.
Note: always check the drum temperature before charging.

# Glossary
**First crack** is the audible popping when steam escapes the bean.
**Charge** is the moment green coffee enters the hot drum.
**Drop** is the moment roasted coffee leaves the drum.
**Bloom** is the release of carbon dioxide when water first touches fresh grounds.
**Chaff** is the papery skin that separates from the bean during roasting.
Note: always check the drum temperature before charging.
**Drop** is the moment roasted coffee leaves the drum.

We buy from three producing regions. Each lot is cupped before purchase, following ![[r007-cupping]].

Huila lots are balanced, with red apple and panela sweetness. They work as filter and as [[espresso#Espresso]].

Cerrado naturals are nutty and low in acidity. They form the base of the house blend described in [blends hakkında](blends.md).

# Filter Coffee
Filter coffee uses a 1:16 ratio of coffee to water.
## Pour over
- Rinse the paper filter.
- Bloom with twice the coffee weight in water for 30 seconds.
- Pour in slow circles until the target weight.

# Cupping
Cupping is the standard tasting protocol used to evaluate lots.
## Protocol
1. Grind 8.25 g of coffee per 150 ml of water.
2. Smell the dry grounds.
3. Pour water at 93 °C and wait four minutes.
4. Break the crust and skim.
5. Slurp from a spoon and score.
## Scoring
Scores cover fragrance, flavor, aftertaste, acidity, body and balance. Lots under 84 points are rejected. Results are stored next to the [[r013-r005-roast-log|roast-log notu]].

Chaff can ignite. Keep a class D extinguisher next to the roaster and never leave a batch unattended.
## Burns
The drum and the steam wand are hot. Use gloves when emptying the cooling tray.

# Roasting
Roasting turns green coffee into the brown beans we grind. The roaster controls heat, airflow and time, and every batch is logged in [[r018-r013-r005-roast-log#Roast Log]].
## Stages
1. Drying: moisture leaves the bean until it turns yellow.
2. Maillard: sugars and amino acids react and aromas develop. - The bean expands and the color moves to tan. - Most body is built here.
3. Development: the time after first crack that sets acidity.
## Profiles
Light profiles keep floral notes and are used for [[r014-origins]]. Dark profiles mute acidity and suit ![[espresso]].
> Never roast two origins in the same drum without a cleaning cycle.
Note: always check the drum temperature before charging.

# Grinders
Burr grinders give a consistent particle size. Flat burrs are used for [espresso](espresso.md) and conical burrs for filter.
## Calibration
Grind size is adjusted daily. A finer grind slows the shot, a coarser grind speeds it up.
## Cleaning
Grinders are cleaned weekly with rice-free cleaning tablets.

# Safety
Roasting produces smoke and heat; the exhaust must be inspected according to [[r019-r016-r008-r004-maintenance]].
## Fire
Chaff can ignite. Keep a class D extinguisher next to the roaster and never leave a batch unattended.
## Burns
The drum and the steam wand are hot. Use gloves when emptying the cooling tray.
Emergency number: 112

We buy from three producing regions. Each lot is cupped before purchase, following ![[r017-r007-cupping]].

Cerrado naturals are nutty and low in acidity. They form the base of the house blend described in [blends hakkında](blends.md).

# Espresso
Espresso is brewed with nine bars of pressure for about 28 seconds.
## Recipe
- Dose: 18 g
- Yield: 36 g
- Time: 26 to 30 seconds - Under 24 seconds tastes sour. - Over 32 seconds tastes bitter.
## Equipment
The shop uses a two-group machine that is descaled every month according to [maintenance hakkında](r019-r016-r008-r004-maintenance.md).

```python
def ratio(dose, yield_):
    return yield_ / dose  # 1:2 is the house standard
```
The house blend is defined in [[blends]].

Roasting produces smoke and heat; the exhaust must be inspected according to [[r019-r016-r008-r004-maintenance]].
## Fire
Chaff can ignite. Keep a class D extinguisher next to the roaster and never leave a batch unattended.
## Burns
The drum and the steam wand are hot. Use gloves when emptying the cooling tray.
Emergency number: 112
Last reviewed by the technician.

# Cupping
Cupping is the standard tasting protocol used to evaluate lots.
## Protocol
1. Grind 8.25 g of coffee per 150 ml of water.
2. Smell the dry grounds.
3. Pour water at 93 °C and wait four minutes.
4. Break the crust and skim.
5. Slurp from a spoon and score.
## Scoring
Scores cover fragrance, flavor, aftertaste, acidity, body and balance. Lots under 84 points are rejected. Results are stored next to the [[r018-r013-r005-roast-log|roast-log notu]].

# Origins
We buy from three producing regions. Each lot is cupped before purchase, following ![[r017-r007-cupping]].
## Ethiopia
Guji and Yirgacheffe lots are washed and show jasmine and bergamot. They are roasted light, see ![[r021-r011-roasting]].
## Colombia
Huila lots are balanced, with red apple and panela sweetness. They work as filter and as [[r024-espresso#Espresso]].
## Brazil
Cerrado naturals are nutty and low in acidity. They form the base of the house blend described in [blends hakkında](blends.md).

# Espresso
Espresso is brewed with nine bars of pressure for about 28 seconds.
## Recipe
- Dose: 18 g
- Yield: 36 g
- Time: 26 to 30 seconds - Under 24 seconds tastes sour. - Over 32 seconds tastes bitter.
## Equipment
The shop uses a two-group machine that is descaled every month according to [maintenance hakkında](r019-r016-r008-r004-maintenance.md).

```python
def ratio(dose, yield_):
    return yield_ / dose  # 1:2 is the house standard
```
The house blend is defined in [[blends]].

# Filter Coffee
Filter coffee uses a 1:16 ratio of coffee to water.
## Pour over
- Rinse the paper filter.
- Bloom with twice the coffee weight in water for 30 seconds.
- Pour in slow circles until the target weight.
Colombian lots from [r026-r014-origins](r026-r014-origins.md) are the default filter offering. The grinder setting is described in [grinders hakkında](r022-r002-grinders.md).

# Cupping
Cupping is the standard tasting protocol used to evaluate lots.
## Protocol
1. Grind 8.25 g of coffee per 150 ml of water.
2. Smell the dry grounds.
3. Pour water at 93 °C and wait four minutes.
4. Break the crust and skim.
5. Slurp from a spoon and score.
## Scoring
Scores cover fragrance, flavor, aftertaste, acidity, body and balance. Lots under 84 points are rejected. Results are stored next to the [[r028-r018-r013-r005-roast-log|roast-log notu]].

**Chaff** is the papery skin that separates from the bean during roasting.

# Origins
We buy from three producing regions. Each lot is cupped before purchase, following ![[r030-r017-r007-cupping]].
## Ethiopia
Guji and Yirgacheffe lots are washed and show jasmine and bergamot. They are roasted light, see ![[r021-r011-roasting]].
## Colombia
Huila lots are balanced, with red apple and panela sweetness. They work as filter and as [[r027-r024-espresso#Espresso]].
## Brazil
Cerrado naturals are nutty and low in acidity. They form the base of the house blend described in [blends hakkında](blends.md).

Burr grinders give a consistent particle size. Flat burrs are used for [r027-r024-espresso](r027-r024-espresso.md) and conical burrs for filter.
## Calibration
Grind size is adjusted daily. A finer grind slows the shot, a coarser grind speeds it up.
## Cleaning
Grinders are cleaned weekly with rice-free cleaning tablets.

# Espresso
Espresso is brewed with nine bars of pressure for about 28 seconds.
## Recipe
- Dose: 18 g
- Yield: 36 g
- Time: 26 to 30 seconds - Under 24 seconds tastes sour. - Over 32 seconds tastes bitter.
## Equipment
The shop uses a two-group machine that is descaled every month according to [maintenance hakkında](r019-r016-r008-r004-maintenance.md).

```python
def ratio(dose, yield_):
    return yield_ / dose  # 1:2 is the house standard
```
The house blend is defined in [[blends]].

# Glossary
**First crack** is the audible popping when steam escapes the bean.
**Charge** is the moment green coffee enters the hot drum.
**Drop** is the moment roasted coffee leaves the drum.
**Bloom** is the release of carbon dioxide when water first touches fresh grounds.
**Chaff** is the papery skin that separates from the bean during roasting.
Note: always check the drum temperature before charging.
**Drop** is the moment roasted coffee leaves the drum.

# Origins
We buy from three producing regions. Each lot is cupped before purchase, following ![[r030-r017-r007-cupping]].
## Ethiopia
Guji and Yirgacheffe lots are washed and show jasmine and bergamot. They are roasted light, see ![[r021-r011-roasting]].
## Colombia
Huila lots are balanced, with red apple and panela sweetness. They work as filter and as [[r034-r027-r024-espresso#Espresso]].
## Brazil
Cerrado naturals are nutty and low in acidity. They form the base of the house blend described in [blends hakkında](r036-blends.md).

# Maintenance
Regular maintenance keeps the equipment safe.
## Daily
- Backflush the espresso machine with a blind basket.
- Empty the chaff collector of the roaster.
## Monthly
- Descale the espresso machine boiler.
- Inspect the roaster exhaust for build-up.
Note: always check the drum temperature before charging.

# Espresso
Espresso is brewed with nine bars of pressure for about 28 seconds.
## Recipe
- Dose: 18 g
- Yield: 36 g
- Time: 26 to 30 seconds - Under 24 seconds tastes sour. - Over 32 seconds tastes bitter.
## Equipment
The shop uses a two-group machine that is descaled every month according to [maintenance hakkında](r038-r019-r016-r008-r004-maintenance.md).

# Safety
Roasting produces smoke and heat; the exhaust must be inspected according to [[r038-r019-r016-r008-r004-maintenance]].
## Fire
Chaff can ignite. Keep a class D extinguisher next to the roaster and never leave a batch unattended.
## Burns
The drum and the steam wand are hot. Use gloves when emptying the cooling tray.

# Roasting
Roasting turns green coffee into the brown beans we grind. The roaster controls heat, airflow and time, and every batch is logged in [[r041-r028-r018-r013-r005-roast-log#Roast Log]].
## Stages
1. Drying: moisture leaves the bean until it turns yellow.
2. Maillard: sugars and amino acids react and aromas develop. - The bean expands and the color moves to tan. - Most body is built here.
3. Development: the time after first crack that sets acidity.
## Profiles
Light profiles keep floral notes and are used for [[r037-r026-r014-origins]]. Dark profiles mute acidity and suit ![[r039-r034-r027-r024-espresso]].
> Never roast two origins in the same drum without a cleaning cycle.
Note: always check the drum temperature before charging.

Roasting produces smoke and heat; the exhaust must be inspected according to [[r038-r019-r016-r008-r004-maintenance]].

Chaff can ignite. Keep a class D extinguisher next to the roaster and never leave a batch unattended.

The drum and the steam wand are hot. Use gloves when emptying the cooling tray.

Burr grinders give a consistent particle size. Flat burrs are used for [r039-r034-r027-r024-espresso](r039-r034-r027-r024-espresso.md) and conical burrs for filter.

Grind size is adjusted daily. A finer grind slows the shot, a coarser grind speeds it up.
## Cleaning
Grinders are cleaned weekly with rice-free cleaning tablets.

# Maintenance
Regular maintenance keeps the equipment safe.
## Daily
- Backflush the espresso machine with a blind basket.
- Empty the chaff collector of the roaster.
## Monthly
- Descale the espresso machine boiler.
- Inspect the roaster exhaust for build-up.
Note: always check the drum temperature before charging.

Morning shifts start at seven. The roaster runs batches on Tuesday and Friday.

# Cupping
Cupping is the standard tasting protocol used to evaluate lots.
## Protocol
1. Grind 8.25 g of coffee per 150 ml of water.
2. Smell the dry grounds.
3. Pour water at 93 °C and wait four minutes.
4. Break the crust and skim.
5. Slurp from a spoon and score.
## Scoring
Scores cover fragrance, flavor, aftertaste, acidity, body and balance. Lots under 84 points are rejected. Results are stored next to the [[r041-r028-r018-r013-r005-roast-log|roast-log notu]].

Grinders are cleaned weekly with rice-free cleaning tablets.

# Cupping
Cupping is the standard tasting protocol used to evaluate lots.
## Protocol
1. Grind 8.25 g of coffee per 150 ml of water.
2. Smell the dry grounds.
3. Pour water at 93 °C and wait four minutes.
4. Break the crust and skim.
5. Slurp from a spoon and score.
## Scoring
Scores cover fragrance, flavor, aftertaste, acidity, body and balance. Lots under 84 points are rejected. Results are stored next to the [[r041-r028-r018-r013-r005-roast-log|roast-log notu]].

# Glossary
**First crack** is the audible popping when steam escapes the bean.
**Charge** is the moment green coffee enters the hot drum.
**Drop** is the moment roasted coffee leaves the drum.
**Bloom** is the release of carbon dioxide when water first touches fresh grounds.
**Chaff** is the papery skin that separates from the bean during roasting.
Note: always check the drum temperature before charging.
**Drop** is the moment roasted coffee leaves the drum.

# Espresso
Espresso is brewed with nine bars of pressure for about 28 seconds.
## Recipe
- Dose: 18 g
- Yield: 36 g
- Time: 26 to 30 seconds - Under 24 seconds tastes sour. - Over 32 seconds tastes bitter.
## Equipment
The shop uses a two-group machine that is descaled every month according to [maintenance hakkında](r046-r045-r038-r019-r016-r008-r004-maintenance.md).

```python
def ratio(dose, yield_):
    return yield_ / dose  # 1:2 is the house standard
```
The house blend is defined in [[r050-r036-blends]].

# Cupping
Cupping is the standard tasting protocol used to evaluate lots.
## Protocol
1. Grind 8.25 g of coffee per 150 ml of water.
2. Smell the dry grounds.
3. Pour water at 93 °C and wait four minutes.
4. Break the crust and skim.
5. Slurp from a spoon and score.
## Scoring
Scores cover fragrance, flavor, aftertaste, acidity, body and balance. Lots under 84 points are rejected. Results are stored next to the [[r041-r028-r018-r013-r005-roast-log|roast-log notu]].
